newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia local poll needs stricter monitoring - Bildt.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia local poll needs stricter monitoring - Bildt.

text.p: International peace mediator Carl Bildt says Bosnia's hotly-contested local elections will require stricter independent supervision than national balloting held last month.

Municipal elections in Bosnia are scheduled for November 22-24 but some diplomats say international organisers need more time to correct problems which appeared in the September 14 vote for national offices.

"Small divergencies have a larger impact on (the local) election result. That means there must be a higher standard for the local elections than for the national ones," Bildt, the International High Representative to Bosnia, told reporters on Wednesday.
Bildt spoke after meeting envoys from countries in the Bosnian peace "implementation council", which includes the United States, European Union states, Russia and Japan.
He said the envoys called for international monitoring of all polling stations during and after the vote as well as provisions for recounts if necessary.
"We have also stressed the fact that there must be international supervision at all of the polling stations and (supervision) throughout the counting process of the ballots," he said.
Bildt acknowledged there was little time to prepare for the local elections less than two months away.
"That means that in order to meet these conditions within that short time frame we have to go that extra mile in terms of efforts," Bildt said.
"But it is demanding, yes it is."

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which has the task of supervising the local elections, came under criticism from opposition parties and independent analysts for its handling of the September poll.

Critics said the OSCE failed to account for an extraordinarily high voter turnout and shied away from using its authority to punish violations of the Dayton peace accord, which required the vote be held under "free and fair" conditions.
The chief of a team of independent election observers, Ed Van Thijn, has recommended the OSCE delay the local elections until next year.
Russian envoy Alexander Axenenok, who attended the council meeting with Bildt, said European officials in the OSCE sharply disagreed with a U.S. envoy about the timing of the local elections.

OSCE officials told Robert Frowick, the American diplomat heading the OSCE mission in Bosnia, they had serious doubts about the wisdom of holding the elections so soon after the national poll, Axenenok said.
"Frowick seemed not too convincing when telling us that November elections were feasible, in practical terms," Axenonok said.
Flavio Cotti, the chairman-in-office of the OSCE, made clear to Frowick that he disagreed with the timing of the vote, Axenoonok said. "He (Cotti) said so openly."
"Frowick has no support in the OSCE. Formally he can go ahead without this support, but we're afraid it may have serious implications for the peace process," he added.
Frowick and other U.S. officials say elections, however imperfect, should be held as soon as possible to create post-war legal institutions.
Delaying national or local elections would create a political vacuum that could cause instability and threaten the success of the U.S.-brokered peace agreement, they say.
